name: BRELSFORD RES (DIANA)
address: 1312 NW DISCOVERY PARK DRIVE, BEND, OR 97703

fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entry clearly to indicate it is the only vehicle access point to the property.
• Post the address number on the detached structure as well as the main residence so responders can identify each building separately.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Install a gate or fence opening at the rear of the property to give responders a secondary way to reach the back of the lot on foot.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked or secured with a lock-box so responders can open it without delay.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of overnight or long-term parked vehicles that would block driveway turnaround space for emergency apparatus.
• Trim shrubs and low-hanging tree branches along the driveway to maintain clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Mark or number each structure visibly from the driveway so arriving responders can immediately distinguish the main residence from the detached structure.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored materials or equipment that would prevent responders from using it as a staging area.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the house to create open space between the plants and the exterior walls.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing close to the base of the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the house so they are not touching or leaning against the building.
• Keep shrubs separated from each other so fire cannot move easily from one plant to the next toward the house.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape areas by keeping plants pruned and free of dead material.
• Mark the single access route clearly so it is easy to find and navigate, particularly in low visibility or smoky conditions.
• Keep the access route free of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along both sides.
• Avoid parking vehicles or storing materials on or along the access route so it stays clear for emergency use.
